> **Relation to #61601.** #61601 fixed the *write* side of the PLE state in align mode: the boundary checkpoints of the PLE group are now written, so the blocks stored in the prefix cache, offloaded to CPU/disk or sent over PD hold the correct conv state. This PR fixes the *read* side, which is still broken on `main`: when a request resumes from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector load or PD transfer), the PLE reads its initial conv state from the wrong block and never sees the state that was loaded. The original version of this PR fixed both halves; after rebasing on #61601 only the read-side fix remains.

## Purpose

Fix the PLE (per-layer n-gram embedding) short-conv state handling of `qwen4_exp` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) in `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, so that a request resumed from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector loads, PD) reads the conv state that was loaded for it.

Part of the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next tracking issue #55922 (KV offload section). Same component as #59642 (PD side of the PLE state). Possibly related symptoms: #55357 (episodic 0% MTP acceptance with prefix caching on), #53912.

## Root cause

In align mode the PLE metadata builder (`short_conv_attn.py`) takes `block_table[:, 0]` of the align-gathered block table, i.e. the block of the last *scheduled* token, and uses it both to read the initial conv state and to write the final one. The Mamba/GDN backends instead receive `block_idx_last_computed_token` and read the resumed state from the block of the last *computed* token inside their kernels; the PLE conv kernel has no align support at all.

Two consequences:

1. A request resumed at, say, 6400 computed tokens with 3714 new tokens has its loaded state in block 1 but the PLE reads block 3, which was just allocated and never written. When that memory contains NaN the NaN appears in the PLE output of layer 1 with clean inputs and poisons the whole model; when it contains finite garbage the state is silently wrong.
2. Before #61601, blocks that end at a 3200-token boundary crossed by a prefill chunk were never written, so the prefix cache and the offloading tiers stored uninitialized memory for the PLE group (inspecting the stored blocks showed NaN in the PLE slot of every block of that group). #61601 fixes this one.

GPU-local flows (chunked prefill, local prefix hits) are not affected because the KV cache manager copies the state forward for them (`_apply_cow`); external loads only extend the block table (`allocate_external_computed_blocks`), so consequence 1 is still present on `main` after #61601.

## Changes

- `short_conv_attn.py`: in align mode compute per row the carry source (block holding the state after the computed tokens) and destination (block the kernels address). Decode and spec rows go into persistent builder buffers padded with `NULL_BLOCK_ID`, like `spec_state_indices_tensor`, so full CUDA graph replay reads valid indices.
- `ple_layer.py`: copy the conv state from source to destination before each conv (decode, spec and prefill paths), and after a prefill zero the speculative scratch columns of the addressed block so stored blocks never carry garbage. Boundary checkpoints are left to #61601's exporter.

No behavior change when `mamba_cache_mode != "align"`: the new metadata fields stay `None` and the layer code paths are skipped.

## Test Plan

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4 on DGX Spark (GB10, 119 GiB unified memory), `OffloadingConnector` with `TieringOffloadingSpec` (CPU tier + fs secondary tier), `mamba_cache_mode=align`, MTP k=3, prefix caching on, 8 GiB GPU KV cache. Load: 48 conversations of ~10.1k tokens (3200 shared system prompt + 6600 per-conversation context), 256 requests at concurrency 4, so most prefix hits come from the offloading tiers (6400-token external hits, ~49% of prompt tokens overall). A per-layer NaN probe was injected for the diagnostic runs.

## Test Result

**Rebased version (carry only, boundary checkpoints from #61601), revalidated October 21** with an image built from this branch (`0.1.dev23462+g40c4e605b`, no file injection) on a GB300 Station, TP=1, MTP k=3, CPU tier 4 GiB + NVMe tier, 256 requests: no errors, 1134 chunk hits served from the NVMe tier, 49.4% external prefix hits, MTP acceptance 2.12 on average and flat from 0% to 49% hits (2.08-2.21 per window), median TTFT 0.94 s first occurrence vs 0.43 s repeated. Unit tests: the new `test_ple_align_carry_blocks` (all-spec, mixed and non-spec batches, with and without full CUDA graphs, CUDA sync debug mode on) and `test_ple_carry_state_copies_from_computed_block`, plus the existing `test_ple_metadata_preserves_request_and_token_order`: 19 passed on GB300.

The numbers below were measured with the original version (carry + own checkpoint writer) on the pre-#61601 base.

Validated at TP=1 on two single-GPU hosts (GB10 and GB300). Not applicable to multi-node TP, for a reason unrelated to this fix (see below).

| run (GB10) | fix | external hits | NaN in model | MTP acceptance | stored PLE blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=2 baseline | no | 31% | yes, born in PLE layer 1 on resumed prefills | 2.2 -> 1.0 as hits start | NaN in PLE slot |
| TP=1 | no | 49% | none (uninitialized memory happened to be finite) | 2.13 | NaN in PLE slot |
| TP=1 | yes | 49% | none, 17,751 probe records | 2.19 | fully initialized, scratch zeroed |
| TP=1, tier on local NVMe | yes | 49% | none | 2.18 | fully initialized |
| GB300 Station, TP=1, CPU tier 32 GiB + NVMe tier | yes | 49% | none | 2.12 | fully initialized |
| GB300 Station, TP=1, CPU tier 4 GiB so hits are promoted from NVMe (1134 chunk hits from the fs tier) | yes | 49% | none | 2.08 | fully initialized |

The stored-block inspection is the direct evidence for the write side of the fix: before, the PLE slot of every stored block of that KV group contained uninitialized memory; after, it holds the boundary state with the three speculative columns zeroed. The TP=1-without-fix row shows why the bug can hide: the engine reads the wrong block either way, and only shows symptoms when that memory happens to hold NaN.

On a GB300 Station (256 GB HBM, 494 GB DRAM, local NVMe) the same load shows the expected gain with the fix in place: median TTFT 0.81 s for first occurrences vs 0.31 s for repeated conversations with hits served from the CPU tier, and 0.97 s vs 0.36 s when the CPU tier is shrunk to 4 GiB so that hits are promoted from the NVMe tier; MTP acceptance stays at 2.1 throughout. Before the fix the same hits made it collapse to 1.0.

Revalidated after rebasing on `main` (371745ebd6, after #58114 and #58997) with an image built from this branch, no file injection: GB300 Station, TP=1, MTP k=3, CPU tier 4 GiB + NVMe tier, 256 requests. No errors (the all-speculative decode path that the earlier rebase broke runs on every steady-state step), 1134 chunk hits served from the NVMe tier, 49% external prefix hits, MTP acceptance 2.12 on average (2.02-2.20 per window, flat from 0% to 49% hits), median TTFT 0.90 s first occurrence vs 0.40 s repeated. Note that on current `main` `--mamba-cache-mode` is deprecated and align mode follows `--enable-prefix-caching`, so this path is active by default whenever prefix caching is on.

TTFT on GB10 at TP=1 does not improve with offloading (10.5 s first occurrence vs 11.1 s repeat, both on NFS and on local NVMe) because the 99 GiB model leaves the node memory-starved (host<->GPU copies at 200 MB/s versus 56 GB/s on an idle node, prefill at ~750 tok/s); that is a platform limit of this model on a single GB10, not a property of the fix.

TP=2 on GB10 means multi-node TP (one GPU per node), and there the tiering manager runs in the scheduler process on rank 0's node and only sees that node's mmap region: only `_r0` files are ever written, rank 1 never creates the secondary tier, and on a load rank 1 copies a stale slot from its own `/dev/shm`. The result is wrong but finite KV on rank 1 (0 NaN in the layer probe, MTP acceptance collapses to 1.0 as soon as external hits start), with or without this fix and with or without #58413. That is the single-host assumption of #54415 (addressed by #46556); details posted there. A TP=2 validation of this fix needs a single host with two GPUs.

**What changed.** The version you patched in (October 9) had a bug in the all-speculative decode path: on a recent vLLM with MTP it raises `UnboundLocalError` on the first all-spec step (reported in review above). Since you saw garbage rather than a crash, the patched files were probably not the ones being imported, or your base predates the change that exposed it; either way the run doesn't tell us much about the fix. Separately, #61601 (merged October 19) now writes the PLE boundary checkpoints, which was the other half of the original PR. This PR has been rebased on top of it and now only fixes the read side, with tests.

**Why your setup can hit the read-side bug.** The LMCache MP connector supports Mamba align mode and loads the recurrent state into the request's blocks the same way the native OffloadingConnector does. On `main`, an external load only extends the block table (`allocate_external_computed_blocks`, no copy), while the PLE reads its initial conv state from the block of the last scheduled token. So with your 32.8% external hit rate, every request resumed from LMCache starts its PLE conv from the wrong block. That is connector-agnostic, and it matches what we saw with the native offloading tiers: MTP acceptance dropping to 0 and degenerate output on resumed requests only.

**What doesn't fit yet.** You also see it without MTP and most of your hits are local (97.6% prefix hit rate), so there may be a second cause. Two candidates: your image predates #61601, so PLE checkpoints at prefix-cache boundaries were not written correctly; and `--prefix-match-unit 16` lets hits land inside a physical block, which I haven't traced end to end for the PLE.

Could you try these, one at a time, with the same traffic?
1. Same config without `--kv-transfer-config` (no LMCache). If the garbage persists, LMCache and the external-load path are not involved.
2. With LMCache, without `--prefix-match-unit` (default granularity).
3. A recent `main` (after #61601) with this PR applied: the rebased branch is `aijanai/vllm:amassidda/ple-align-state-fix`. It would also help to know the vLLM commit your image is built from. Thanks!

Closing this as superseded by #61601. Summary for anyone landing here from the PLE state corruption:

- **The bug.** With `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next requests resumed from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector loads, PD transfers) ran on a corrupted PLE short-conv state. The PLE checkpoint blocks at the cacheable boundaries were never written, so the prefix cache and the offloading tiers stored uninitialized memory for the PLE group, and the resumed request started from it. With NaN in that memory, MTP acceptance collapsed from ~2.2 to 1.0 as soon as external hits started (measured on GB10 and GB300). This PR identified it and fixed it on October 9 by writing the boundary checkpoints and carrying the state into the block the kernel reads.
- **Why it is no longer needed.** #61601 (internal prefill checkpoints for the PLE short conv, merged October 20) makes the PLE export its conv window at the checkpoint, which writes exactly the blocks that were left uninitialized. The read side was already covered on `main`: in align mode MRV2's `preprocess_state` (`model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`) copies every Mamba state, including the PLE short conv via `short_conv_state_copy_func`, from the block of the last computed token to the block the kernels address before the forward. So the carry in this PR duplicates an existing copy.
- **Verification on `main` (9d4192aaa1) without this PR**, GB300 Station, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, TP=1, MTP k=3, OffloadingConnector with CPU + NVMe tiers:
  - offloading lab, 256 requests up to 49% external prefix hits: no errors, MTP acceptance flat at 2.11 (2.12 with this PR);
  - state probe on every resumed prefill (chunked prefill and loads from the tier): the initial conv state the PLE kernel reads matches the state after the computed tokens bit for bit (48/48 rows, max abs diff 0, no NaN, no zeroed blocks), with or without the carry.
- **One open point.** The #61601 description says the PLE checkpoints are only exported where #60050's are (FlashInfer GDN prefill, prefix caching on); our runs used the FlashInfer GDN prefill. I have not checked whether the PLE boundary blocks are written when those checkpoints are off; if they are not, the corruption described above would come back in that configuration, and I will open a separate issue if a probe shows it.

Thanks @EagleClaw89 for the review that caught the all-spec `UnboundLocalError`.

Follow-up on the open point: also checked with `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` (no internal prefill checkpoints). On every resumed prefill, from chunked prefill and from offload-tier loads, the PLE reads exactly the state computed cold at that boundary (48/48 rows, max abs diff 0, no NaN). So no corruption on `main` in either configuration; no issue to open.

`spec_req_idx_cpu` is unbound in the all-speculative branch of `build()`.

After #58114 ("Reduce PLE metadata construction overhead", merged 2026-09-28), `spec_req_idx_cpu = spec_sequence_masks_cpu.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]` is assigned only in the mixed-batch `else:` branch of `short_conv_attn.py`. This PR's new call

```python
align_fields = self._ple_align_fields(
    m,
    decode_req_idx_cpu if num_decodes > 0 else None,
    prefill_req_idx_cpu if num_prefills > 0 else None,
    spec_req_idx_cpu if num_spec_decodes > 0 else None, ...
```

It fires in every cache mode, not only align.

```
short_conv_attn.py", line 571, in build
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'spec_req_idx_cpu'

```diff
@@ -424,6 +424,8 @@
         non_spec_req_idx: torch.Tensor | None = None
 
+        spec_req_idx_cpu = spec_sequence_masks_cpu.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
         if num_decodes == 0 and num_prefills == 0:
@@ -440,7 +442,6 @@

-            spec_req_idx_cpu = spec_sequence_masks_cpu.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
             decode_req_idx_cpu = decode_mask_cpu.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]
```

(The PR's `test_ple.py` spec-padding case is a pure-spec batch and should hit the same path.) Not yet checked: whether the full engine then decodes correctly with the PR; our confidence is on the boot path only.

Load: 48 conversations of ~10.1k tokens (3200 shared system prompt + 6600 per-conversation context), 256 requests at concurrency 4, so most prefix hits come from the offloading tiers (6400-token external hits, ~49% of prompt tokens overall). A per-layer NaN probe was injected for the diagnostic runs.

## Test Result

**Rebased version (carry only, boundary checkpoints from #61601), revalidated October 21** with an image built from this branch (`0.1.dev23462+g40c4e605b`, no file injection) on a GB300 Station, TP=1, MTP k=3, CPU tier 4 GiB + NVMe tier, 256 requests: no errors, 1134 chunk hits served from the NVMe tier, 49.4% external prefix hits, MTP acceptance 2.12 on average and flat from 0% to 49% hits (2.08-2.21 per window), median TTFT 0.94 s first occurrence vs 0.43 s repeated. Unit tests: the new `test_ple_align_carry_blocks` (all-spec, mixed and non-spec batches, with and without full CUDA graphs, CUDA sync debug mode on) and `test_ple_carry_state_copies_from_computed_block`, plus the existing `test_ple_metadata_preserves_request_and_token_order`: 19 passed on GB300.

The numbers below were measured with the original version (carry + own checkpoint writer) on the pre-#61601 base.

Validated at TP=1 on two single-GPU hosts (GB10 and GB300). Not applicable to multi-node TP, for a reason unrelated to this fix (see below).

| run (GB10) | fix | external hits | NaN in model | MTP acceptance | stored PLE blocks |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP=2 baseline | no | 31% | yes, born in PLE layer 1 on resumed prefills | 2.2 -> 1.0 as hits start | NaN in PLE slot |
| TP=1 | no | 49% | none (uninitialized memory happened to be finite) | 2.13 | NaN in PLE slot |
| TP=1 | yes | 49% | none, 17,751 probe records | 2.19 | fully initialized, scratch zeroed |
| TP=1, tier on local NVMe | yes | 49% | none | 2.18 | fully initialized |
| GB300 Station, TP=1, CPU tier 32 GiB + NVMe tier | yes | 49% | none | 2.12 | fully initialized |
| GB300 Station, TP=1, CPU tier 4 GiB so hits are promoted from NVMe (1134 chunk hits from the fs tier) | yes | 49% | none | 2.08 | fully initialized |

The stored-block inspection is the direct evidence for the write side of the fix: before, the PLE slot of every stored block of that KV group contained uninitialized memory; after, it holds the boundary state with the three speculative columns zeroed. The TP=1-without-fix row shows why the bug can hide: the engine reads the wrong block either way, and only shows symptoms when that memory happens to hold NaN.

On a GB300 Station (256 GB HBM, 494 GB DRAM, local NVMe) the same load shows the expected gain with the fix in place: median TTFT 0.81 s for first occurrences vs 0.31 s for repeated conversations with hits served from the CPU tier, and 0.97 s vs 0.36 s when the CPU tier is shrunk to 4 GiB so that hits are promoted from the NVMe tier; MTP acceptance stays at 2.1 throughout. Before the fix the same hits made it collapse to 1.0.

Revalidated after rebasing on `main` (371745ebd6, after #58114 and #58997) with an image built from this branch, no file injection: GB300 Station, TP=1, MTP k=3, CPU tier 4 GiB + NVMe tier, 256 requests. No errors (the all-speculative decode path that the earlier rebase broke runs on every steady-state step), 1134 chunk hits served from the NVMe tier, 49% external prefix hits, MTP acceptance 2.12 on average (2.02-2.20 per window, flat from 0% to 49% hits), median TTFT 0.90 s first occurrence vs 0.40 s repeated. Note that on current `main` `--mamba-cache-mode` is deprecated and align mode follows `--enable-prefix-caching`, so this path is active by default whenever prefix caching is on.

TTFT on GB10 at TP=1 does not improve with offloading (10.5 s first occurrence vs 11.1 s repeat, both on NFS and on local NVMe) because the 99 GiB model leaves the node memory-starved (host<->GPU copies at 200 MB/s versus 56 GB/s on an idle node, prefill at ~750 tok/s); that is a platform limit of this model on a single GB10, not a property of the fix.

TP=2 on GB10 means multi-node TP (one GPU per node), and there the tiering manager runs in the scheduler process on rank 0's node and only sees that node's mmap region: only `_r0` files are ever written, rank 1 never creates the secondary tier, and on a load rank 1 copies a stale slot from its own `/dev/shm`. The result is wrong but finite KV on rank 1 (0 NaN in the layer probe, MTP acceptance collapses to 1.0 as soon as external hits start), with or without this fix and with or without #58413. That is the single-host assumption of #54415 (addressed by #46556); details posted there. A TP=2 validation of this fix needs a single host with two GPUs.

`spec_req_idx_cpu` is unbound in the all-speculative branch of `build()`.

After #58114 ("Reduce PLE metadata construction overhead", merged 2026-09-28), `spec_req_idx_cpu = spec_sequence_masks_cpu.nonzero(as_tuple=True)[0]` is assigned only in the mixed-batch `else:` branch of `short_conv_attn.py`. This PR's new call

```python
align_fields = self._ple_align_fields(
    m,
    decode_req_idx_cpu if num_decodes > 0 else None,
    prefill_req_idx_cpu if num_prefills > 0 else None,
    spec_req_idx_cpu if num_spec_decodes > 0 else None, ...
```

runs for every batch. In a pure speculative batch (`num_decodes == 0 and num_prefills == 0`, `num_spec_decodes > 0`, the normal steady state with MTP) the `else:` branch is skipped, so the conditional expression reads an unbound local and raises `UnboundLocalError` before `_ple_align_fields` can check the cache mode. It fires in every cache mode, not only align.

```
short_conv_attn.py", line 571, in build
UnboundLocalError: cannot access local variable 'spec_req_idx_cpu'
```

The PR base is also 453 commits behind main, so a rebase will be needed anyway; the line was hoisted on the base this PR was written against and #58114 moved it.

@SebastianGode thanks for the detailed config, and sorry for the slow follow-up. A few things changed since you tested, and I don't think your test exercised the fix, so here is where things stand and three cheap checks that would tell us which bug you are hitting.

**What changed.** The version you patched in (October 9) had a bug in the all-speculative decode path: on a recent vLLM with MTP it raises `UnboundLocalError` on the first all-spec step (reported in review above). Since you saw garbage rather than a crash, the patched files were probably not the ones being imported, or your base predates the change that exposed it; either way the run doesn't tell us much about the fix. Separately, #61601 (merged October 19) now writes the PLE boundary checkpoints, which was the other half of the original PR. This PR has been rebased on top of it and now only fixes the read side, with tests.

**Why your setup can hit the read-side bug.** The LMCache MP connector supports Mamba align mode and loads the recurrent state into the request's blocks the same way the native OffloadingConnector does. On `main`, an external load only extends the block table (`allocate_external_computed_blocks`, no copy), while the PLE reads its initial conv state from the block of the last scheduled token. So with your 32.8% external hit rate, every request resumed from LMCache starts its PLE conv from the wrong block. That is connector-agnostic, and it matches what we saw with the native offloading tiers: MTP acceptance dropping to 0 and degenerate output on resumed requests only.

**What doesn't fit yet.** You also see it without MTP and most of your hits are local (97.6% prefix hit rate), so there may be a second cause. Two candidates: your image predates #61601, so PLE checkpoints at prefix-cache boundaries were not written correctly; and `--prefix-match-unit 16` lets hits land inside a physical block, which I haven't traced end to end for the PLE.

Could you try these, one at a time, with the same traffic?
1. Same config without `--kv-transfer-config` (no LMCache). If the garbage persists, LMCache and the external-load path are not involved.
2. With LMCache, without `--prefix-match-unit` (default granularity).
3. A recent `main` (after #61601) with this PR applied: the rebased branch is `aijanai/vllm:amassidda/ple-align-state-fix`. The fix is Python-only, so copying `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ple_layer.py` and `vllm/v1/attention/backends/short_conv_attn.py` from that branch is enough, as long as the rest of your tree is at the same `main`.

Closing this as superseded by #61601. Summary for anyone landing here from the PLE state corruption:

- **The bug.** With `mamba_cache_mode="align"`, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next requests resumed from a prefix hit delivered by a KV connector (OffloadingConnector loads, PD transfers) ran on a corrupted PLE short-conv state. The PLE checkpoint blocks at the cacheable boundaries were never written, so the prefix cache and the offloading tiers stored uninitialized memory for the PLE group, and the resumed request started from it. With NaN in that memory, MTP acceptance collapsed from ~2.2 to 1.0 as soon as external hits started (measured on GB10 and GB300). This PR identified it and fixed it on October 9 by writing the boundary checkpoints and carrying the state into the block the kernel reads.
- **Why it is no longer needed.** #61601 (internal prefill checkpoints for the PLE short conv, merged October 20) makes the PLE export its conv window at the checkpoint, which writes exactly the blocks that were left uninitialized. The read side was already covered on `main`: in align mode MRV2's `preprocess_state` (`model_states/mamba_hybrid.py`) copies every Mamba state, including the PLE short conv via `short_conv_state_copy_func`, from the block of the last computed token to the block the kernels address before the forward. So the carry in this PR duplicates an existing copy.
- **Verification on `main` (9d4192aaa1) without this PR**, GB300 Station, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4, TP=1, MTP k=3, OffloadingConnector with CPU + NVMe tiers:
  - offloading lab, 256 requests up to 49% external prefix hits: no errors, MTP acceptance flat at 2.11 (2.12 with this PR);
  - state probe on every resumed prefill (chunked prefill and loads from the tier): the initial conv state the PLE kernel reads matches the state after the computed tokens bit for bit (48/48 rows, max abs diff 0, no NaN, no zeroed blocks), with or without the carry.
- **One open point.** The #61601 description says the PLE checkpoints are only exported where #60050's are (FlashInfer GDN prefill, prefix caching on); our runs used the FlashInfer GDN prefill. I have not checked whether the PLE boundary blocks are written when those checkpoints are off; if they are not, the corruption described above would come back in that configuration, and I will open a separate issue if a probe shows it.

Thanks @EagleClaw89 for the review that caught the all-spec `UnboundLocalError`.

Follow-up on the open point: also checked with `--gdn-prefill-backend triton` (no internal prefill checkpoints). On every resumed prefill, from chunked prefill and from offload-tier loads, the PLE reads exactly the state computed cold at that boundary (48/48 rows, max abs diff 0, no NaN). So no corruption on `main` in either configuration; no issue to open.
